attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 8.8. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pathological stage pT2c, positive surgical margins, and lymphovascular invasion, with no seminal vesicle invasion. A key uncertainty is the nodal status, as no lymph nodes were removed, and missing nodal sampling widens this uncertainty. The difference between biopsy and prostatectomy findings is noted, as the biopsy Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing.

The primary driver for prognosis is the positive margins and lymphovascular invasion. Countervailing factors include the absence of extraprostatic extension and no seminal vesicle invasion. The lack of documented postoperative PSA or follow-up significantly limits the certainty of the trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial to revise this assessment. The current heuristic sensitivity range for recurrence is between 37.7 and 87.9 months.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2c, positive surgical margins, and lymphovascular invasion, with no seminal vesicle invasion. No lymph nodes were removed. Preoperative PSA was 8.8. The surgical pathology report documented "Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pathological stage pT2c. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was present; no lymph nodes were removed."

Prognosis is influenced by the positive surgical margins and the presence of lymphovascular invasion. The absence of documented nodal status, as no lymph nodes were removed, widens the uncertainty regarding regional disease control. The discrepancy between the biopsy and prostatectomy findings, specifically the missing Gleason pattern and ISUP report from the biopsy, also contributes to this uncertainty.

The numeric horizon for recurrence is estimated at 62.79 months, with a heuristic sensitivity range between 37.7 and 87.9 months. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are critical factors that would revise this prognosis. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data prevents a more precise assessment of the disease course.
